findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A zesty orange sauce with “Refrigerate After Opening” was observed on the shelf in the dry storage. CORRECTED - The PIC was educated and the sauce was voluntarily discarded. Ensure time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are stored in the cooler and maintained at 5°C (41°F) or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Disinfectant spray and All purpose cleaner with bleach were observed on the ice machine close to the restroom. CORRECTED - The PIC was educated and the chemicals were voluntarily moved to the chemical storage area. Ensure poisonous or toxic materials are not stored above food or food equipment to prevent chemical contamination of food.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Ice buildup was observed in the silver double door cooler. The PIC was instructed to have the cooler defrosted and cleaned to prevent more ice accumulation. Ensure the cooler is defrosted and cleaned to sight and touch by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Dirty water and the mop head were observed in the mop bucket. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed; the dirty water was discarded, and the mop head was placed in the wringer basket. Ensure mop water is discarded immediately after use and mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer available in the kitchen during food preparation. PIC was informed and a bucket was prepared measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. There was a complication with the initial filling of the bucket in which the concentration read 0ppm. It was discovered that the sanitizer dispenser has to be turned on to its maximum pressure to achieve proper sanitizer concentration. Ensure sanitizer concentration is monitored to guarantee proper sanitizing of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-703.11: Inspector observed the dish machine wash cycle to read 110F and rinse cycle to read 90F. The thermometer run through two cycles of the machine has a surface temperature of 150F. The machine can be used only for cleaning. The sanitize operation can be conducted in the 3 part sink with items left to air dry. The facility will call for the technician to come out to repair the unit. The unit will be followed up on 11/6/24 due to weekend, Holiday and inspector availability. Continue to use the 3 part sink for proper wash, rinse and sanitize as needed.  

After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Inspector observed the cold holding unit in the dinosaur room to be holding food at 50F. A quart and one half of almond milk was discarded in the garbage along with 5 tubes of yogurt. The other items in the unit were shelf stable. The unit is going to be replaced before TCS (Temperature control for safety) foods are added to the room. Until that time keep the foods in the kitchen cooler or other operating cold holding unit. This will be evaluated at the follow up for the dish machine. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: Inspector observed 4 cold holding units to be set at the maximum cold setting and holding food marginally at between 40F and 44F. One unit in Dinosaur has an internal thermometer with a temperature of 60F on the door. The unit needs replaced. This is the unit that food was discarded from. The facility will have a follow up 11/8/24.
EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Inspector observed multiple wet wiping cloths on the counter in the dinosaur room. The cloths were placed in the sanitizer bucket. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer between uses. 

(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: Inspector observed boxes of single use articles on the floor in the kitchen. The boxes were moved up onto crates. Ensure that cleaning is taking place around the crates, or use the shelves for storage. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

(A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: Inspector observed the area behind the stove to have some cracked paint and a dimensional/rectangular hole where mechanicals may have been. The facility replaced the stove and this is now visible. Seal the area so that it is smooth and easily cleanable. 

(A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
